in SUPERINFECTION, ANTI-HBc IgM IS NEGATIVE while anti-HBc IgG is positive (indicating pre-existing chronic HBV), and CHRONIC HDV INFECTION FOLLOWS IN OVER 90%. Note that HDV typically SUPPRESSES HBV REPLICATION, so the HBV DNA level may be low or undetectable even in severe disease - a low HBV DNA in a deteriorating HBsAg-positive patient should therefore RAISE rather than lower suspicion of delta infection. Stage fibrosis with elastography and monitor alpha-fetoprotein and ultrasound

redFlags: FULMINANT HEPATIC FAILURE - HDV coinfection and especially superinfection carry the HIGHEST RISK OF FULMINANT HEPATITIS OF ANY VIRAL HEPATITIS (up to 10-20 times that of HBV alone): watch for encephalopathy, asterixis, an INR above 1.5, hypoglycaemia and a shrinking liver, and refer immediately to a transplant centre. Also urgent: any unexplained flare or clinical deterioration in a known chronic hepatitis B patient - TEST FOR HDV, as this is the classic presentation of superinfection
rapid progression to cirrhosis with decompensation - ascites, variceal bleeding, spontaneous bacterial peritonitis, hepatorenal syndrome or encephalopathy
HEPATOCELLULAR CARCINOMA surveillance every 6 months with ultrasound and alpha-fetoprotein, as the risk is substantially higher than with HBV alone
HIV or HCV coinfection

pregnancy. TREATMENT is difficult and specialist-led - pegylated interferon alfa for at least 48 weeks has limited efficacy, the entry inhibitor BULEVIRTIDE is now approved in some regions, and nucleos(t)ide analogues alone do NOT treat HDV (they treat only the underlying HBV)

liver transplantation is effective for end-stage disease. PREVENTION IS THE KEY MESSAGE - HEPATITIS B VACCINATION PREVENTS HEPATITIS D COMPLETELY, since HDV cannot infect without HBsAg, so ensure universal HBV immunisation, safe injection practice, blood screening and harm reduction for injecting drug users
screen and vaccinate household and sexual contacts

symptoms.sourceText: An acute self-limiting hepatitis clinically indistinguishable from hepatitis A - a prodrome of fever, malaise, anorexia, nausea, vomiting and abdominal pain lasting several days, followed by jaundice, dark urine, pale stools and marked fatigue
The illness usually resolves over 4-6 weeks
Pruritus, which may be prominent as the course is often cholestatic with prolonged jaundice
Most infections, particularly in children, are asymptomatic or anicteric

Extrahepatic manifestations are increasingly recognised, especially with genotype 3, and include GUILLAIN-BARRE syndrome, neuralgic amyotrophy (Parsonage-Turner syndrome), encephalitis, myelitis, glomerulonephritis, cryoglobulinaemia, pancreatitis, thrombocytopenia and aplastic anaemia. epidemiology is the key to suspicion: genotypes 1 and 2 are transmitted by the FAECO-ORAL route through faecally contaminated drinking water, causing large waterborne epidemics in South and Central Asia, the Middle East and Africa, particularly during the rainy season, floods and in refugee and displaced-person camps

Genotypes 3 and 4 are zoonotic, acquired from undercooked pork, wild boar, venison and shellfish, and are the usual cause of sporadic autochthonous cases in high-income countries, chiefly affecting older men
Transfusion transmission and vertical transmission also occur

signs: Jaundice with scleral icterus
smooth tender hepatomegaly
occasional splenomegaly
scratch marks in cholestatic disease

the general condition is usually good in uncomplicated cases, and there are NO STIGMATA OF CHRONIC LIVER DISEASE unless there is pre-existing liver disease. LABORATORY: markedly raised ALT and AST, often in the thousands, with ALT above AST
raised conjugated bilirubin
alkaline phosphatase and GGT are more prominently raised than in hepatitis A because of the cholestatic tendency
CHECK THE PROTHROMBIN TIME/INR IN EVERY PATIENT as the key prognostic marker
monitor glucose. DIAGNOSIS: ANTI-HEV IgM indicates acute infection and is the first-line test, with anti-HEV IgG indicating past exposure
HEV RNA BY PCR in serum or stool confirms active infection and is ESSENTIAL IN IMMUNOCOMPROMISED PATIENTS, IN WHOM SEROLOGY IS UNRELIABLE and may be falsely negative

HEV RNA persisting beyond 3 months defines CHRONIC HEPATITIS E. Exclude other causes with HAV IgM, HBsAg, anti-HBc IgM, anti-HCV, EBV and CMV serology, an autoimmune screen and a drug history, and image the biliary tree with ultrasound

redFlags: PREGNANCY IS THE CRITICAL RED FLAG - HEPATITIS E IN THE THIRD TRIMESTER CARRIES A MATERNAL MORTALITY OF 15-25% from FULMINANT HEPATIC FAILURE, together with a high rate of obstetric haemorrhage, eclampsia, membrane rupture, preterm delivery, stillbirth and neonatal death

any pregnant woman with jaundice in an endemic area must be tested for HEV and managed as high-risk with obstetric and hepatology input. ACUTE LIVER FAILURE - encephalopathy, asterixis, INR above 1.5, hypoglycaemia and a shrinking liver - requires immediate transplant-centre referral

the risk is also markedly increased in those with PRE-EXISTING CHRONIC LIVER DISEASE, in whom HEV superinfection causes ACUTE-ON-CHRONIC LIVER FAILURE with high mortality. CHRONIC HEPATITIS E occurs almost exclusively in the IMMUNOCOMPROMISED - solid organ transplant recipients, patients on chemotherapy or rituximab, and those with advanced HIV - and can progress to cirrhosis within 2-3 years

it requires HEV RNA testing (not serology), reduction of immunosuppression where possible, and RIBAVIRIN therapy. Also refer: neurological complications such as Guillain-Barre syndrome or neuralgic amyotrophy (which may present without jaundice)
persistent vomiting with dehydration
deepening or prolonged cholestatic jaundice
haemolysis in G6PD deficiency

the elderly. PUBLIC HEALTH: notify and investigate the water supply in outbreak settings, ensure safe drinking water, sanitation and hand hygiene, boil or chlorinate water, avoid undercooked pork, boar, venison and shellfish, and note that a vaccine (HEV 239) is licensed in China but not widely available
AVOID ALCOHOL and hepatotoxic drugs during recovery

symptoms.sourceText: Acquired immunodeficiency syndrome is the advanced stage of HIV infection, defined by a CD4 count below 200 CELLS/microlitre or the presence of an AIDS-DEFINING illness. Presenting features are recurrent or opportunistic infections, unexplained weight loss of more than 10% of body weight, prolonged fever for more than a month, chronic diarrhoea for more than a month, and persistent generalised lymphadenopathy

Acute seroconversion illness 2-6 weeks after exposure in 50-90% - a glandular-fever-like illness with fever, sore throat, a non-pruritic maculopapular rash on the trunk, generalised lymphadenopathy, myalgia, headache, mouth ulcers and occasionally aseptic meningitis, which is frequently misdiagnosed. Then a clinically latent phase of years. symptomatic disease: drenching night sweats
Oral thrush and painful swallowing (oesophageal candidiasis)
White corrugated painless plaques on the lateral tongue that cannot be scraped off (oral hairy leukoplakia)
Progressive breathlessness with A dry cough and marked exertional desaturation (Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia)
Chronic cough with fever, night sweats and weight loss (tuberculosis, which is the commonest opportunistic infection and leading cause of death in HIV worldwide)
Headache, fever and neck stiffness with a subacute onset (cryptococcal meningitis)
Focal neurological deficit and seizures (cerebral toxoplasmosis, primary CNS lymphoma)
Progressive cognitive slowing, apathy and gait disturbance (HIV-associated neurocognitive disorder)
Visual floaters and painless progressive visual loss (CMV retinitis)
Painless purple-brown nodules or plaques on the skin, palate or viscera (kaposi sarcoma)
Chronic watery diarrhoea and wasting (cryptosporidiosis, isosporiasis, microsporidiosis, MAC)
Nausea and vomiting (due to opportunistic infections)

signs: GENERAL: cachexia and temporal wasting
oral CANDIDIASIS with white curd-like plaques that scrape off leaving a raw base
ORAL HAIRY LEUKOPLAKIA on the lateral tongue border
angular cheilitis
aphthous ulcers
gingivitis and necrotising periodontitis
generalised LYMPHADENOPATHY involving two or more extra-inguinal sites

hepatosplenomegaly. SKIN: seborrhoeic dermatitis, extensive molluscum contagiosum with large umbilicated lesions in an adult, prurigo nodularis, psoriasis, dermatophytosis, scabies including CRUSTED (Norwegian) scabies, herpes zoster scars, and the violaceous plaques and nodules of KAPOSI SARCOMA. CHEST: often strikingly NORMAL AUSCULTATION IN PNEUMOCYSTIS PNEUMONIA DESPITE MARKED HYPOXIA - always measure oxygen saturation AT REST AND AFTER EXERTION, as exercise desaturation is a key clue

signs of consolidation, effusion or the apical changes of tuberculosis. NEUROLOGICAL: assess for meningism, focal deficits, cranial nerve palsies, papilloedema, cognitive impairment and peripheral neuropathy with absent ankle jerks. EYES: DILATED FUNDOSCOPY for CMV retinitis, which shows perivascular haemorrhages and yellow-white exudates in a 'pizza-pie' or 'cottage cheese and ketchup' pattern - it is sight-threatening and must be sought in anyone with a CD4 below 50. INVESTIGATIONS: HIV ANTIBODY/ANTIGEN (fourth-generation) testing with confirmatory assay, and HIV RNA viral load
CD4 COUNT to stage immunosuppression and guide prophylaxis
full blood count (anaemia, leucopenia, thrombocytopenia are common)
chest radiograph

headache with fever, vomiting or altered consciousness (CRYPTOCOCCAL MENINGITIS - check cryptococcal antigen and measure and repeatedly reduce the RAISED INTRACRANIAL PRESSURE by therapeutic lumbar puncture, which is the single most important determinant of survival
TUBERCULOUS MENINGITIS
toxoplasmosis)
new focal neurological deficit or seizures (imaging before lumbar puncture)
visual symptoms at a low CD4 (CMV retinitis - same-day ophthalmology, as sight loss is irreversible)
disseminated tuberculosis
severe wasting

sepsis. Also urgent: NEWLY DIAGNOSED HIV - START ANTIRETROVIRAL THERAPY PROMPTLY REGARDLESS OF CD4 COUNT, since universal treatment improves survival and renders the person non-infectious to partners (U=U, undetectable equals untransmittable), while TIMING NEEDS CARE IN CRYPTOCOCCAL AND TUBERCULOUS MENINGITIS because of IMMUNE RECONSTITUTION INFLAMMATORY SYNDROME (IRIS), which typically appears within weeks of starting ART as a paradoxical worsening
conditions.firstLine: Initiate antiretroviral therapy promptly regardless of CD4 count, as it significantly improves survival.

symptoms.sourceText: Painful swelling of the parotid gland, usually beginning unilaterally and becoming bilateral in about 70% within a few days
Pain aggravated by chewing, swallowing and by acidic or sour foods and drinks
A prodrome of low-grade fever, headache, malaise, myalgia and anorexia lasting 1-2 days
Trismus and difficulty opening the mouth
symptoms.masterName: Trismus and difficulty opening the mouth

symptoms.sourceText: The face takes on a characteristic appearance with the swelling filling the hollow between the ear lobe and the angle of the jaw and pushing the ear lobe upwards and outwards
The submandibular and sublingual glands may also be involved
Up to a third of infections are asymptomatic or cause only a non-specific respiratory illness
Spread is by respiratory droplets, saliva and fomites
Infectivity extends from about 2 days before to 5 days after the onset of parotid swelling
Outbreaks occur in schools, colleges, military barracks and other crowded settings, including in partially vaccinated populations because of waning immunity

signs: TENDER, DIFFUSE, DOUGHY SWELLING OF THE PAROTID GLAND that obliterates the angle of the mandible and LIFTS THE EAR LOBE UPWARD AND OUTWARD, with overlying skin that is normal or only slightly warm and NOT ERYTHEMATOUS OR INDURATED (in contrast to bacterial suppurative parotitis, in which the gland is exquisitely tender, the skin is red and hot, and PUS CAN BE EXPRESSED FROM STENSEN'S DUCT ON MASSAGE)
the parotid duct orifice opposite the second upper molar is red and oedematous but discharges no pus
trismus
fever of 38-39C

submandibular gland involvement in a minority. EXAMINE THE TESTES IN POST-PUBERTAL MALES for orchitis - a hot, swollen, exquisitely tender testis, usually unilateral, appearing 4-8 days after the parotitis. Examine for meningism, abdominal tenderness (pancreatitis, oophoritis), and hearing. LABORATORY: raised SERUM AMYLASE, which arises from the SALIVARY glands in uncomplicated parotitis (the salivary isoenzyme) and from the pancreas if there is pancreatitis - so a raised amylase alone does not indicate pancreatitis and LIPASE should be measured if pancreatic involvement is suspected
leucopenia with relative lymphocytosis

DIAGNOSIS confirmed by MUMPS IgM SEROLOGY, a fourfold rise in IgG on paired sera, or RT-PCR of a buccal or oral swab taken from the parotid duct region (the preferred test, most sensitive in the first 3 days) or of urine or CSF
note that IgM may be falsely negative in previously vaccinated individuals, so PCR is preferred in that setting
Tender testes in cases of orchitis

Serum amylase and lipase levels if pancreatic involvement is suspected.

redFlags: ORCHITIS occurs in 15-30% of post-pubertal males, is unilateral in about 80% and presents with sudden high fever, rigors, vomiting and severe testicular pain and swelling - it causes some degree of testicular atrophy in about half of affected testes, though STERILITY IS UNCOMMON

nevertheless, the acute scrotum in a young man must be assessed urgently to EXCLUDE TESTICULAR TORSION, which is a surgical emergency requiring intervention within 6 hours. Other complications requiring referral: ASEPTIC MENINGITIS, which occurs in up to 10% and presents with headache, fever, photophobia, vomiting and neck stiffness - usually benign, but lumbar puncture may be needed to exclude bacterial meningitis
ENCEPHALITIS with altered consciousness, seizures or focal deficits (rare but serious)
SUDDEN SENSORINEURAL HEARING LOSS, usually unilateral and often permanent - mumps was historically a leading cause of acquired childhood deafness, so assess hearing and refer promptly
PANCREATITIS with severe epigastric pain radiating to the back, vomiting and a raised lipase
OOPHORITIS with lower abdominal pain in post-pubertal females
myocarditis
nephritis
arthritis
and, in pregnancy, an increased risk of first-trimester miscarriage, although mumps is NOT teratogenic.
referralCriteria: THE PATIENT MUST BE ISOLATED FOR 5 DAYS FROM THE ONSET OF PAROTID SWELLING and excluded from school or work
identify and vaccinate susceptible contacts, though post-exposure vaccination does not reliably prevent disease in that exposure.
conditions.firstLine: treatment is supportive with analgesia, adequate fluids, soft bland non-acidic food and cold or warm compresses

symptoms.sourceText: Risus sardonicus, a fixed sardonic grin from spasm of the facial muscles
Painful generalised muscle spasms precipitated by minimal stimuli
Opisthotonus - arching of the back with hyperextension of the neck and legs during spasms

Spasms triggered by noise, light, touch or any sudden stimulus, which are exquisitely painful and occur with the patient fully conscious - a feature that distinguishes tetanus from seizures and makes the illness terrifying for the patient
A history of a wound in the preceding 3-21 days, which may be trivial or already healed and in up to 20% of cases is never identified - so the absence of an obvious wound never excludes the diagnosis

Classical settings include soil-contaminated puncture wounds, agricultural injury, burns, animal bites, unsafe injection practice, dental infection, otitis media, chronic ulcers, surgery, and neonatal tetanus from unsterile cutting or dressing of the umbilical cord
Inability to suck in neonatal tetanus

signs: The DIAGNOSIS IS ENTIRELY CLINICAL - there is no confirmatory laboratory test, and treatment must never be delayed for investigation. TRISMUS with an inability to open the mouth fully
the SPATULA TEST is useful - touching the posterior pharyngeal wall with a spatula provokes REFLEX MASSETER SPASM AND BITING DOWN in tetanus (a positive test) instead of the normal gag and expulsion
RISUS SARDONICUS from sustained contraction of the facial and perioral muscles
rigid, board-like abdominal muscles
nuchal rigidity
OPISTHOTONUS
generalised tonic spasms lasting seconds to minutes, provoked by stimulation, WITH CONSCIOUSNESS FULLY PRESERVED AND NORMAL SENSORIUM BETWEEN SPASMS
hyperreflexia

AUTONOMIC INSTABILITY appearing in the second week with labile hypertension alternating with hypotension, tachycardia and bradycardia, arrhythmias, profuse sweating, hyperpyrexia and gastric stasis - this is now the leading cause of death in ventilated patients. LOOK CAREFULLY FOR THE ENTRY WOUND, including the ears, umbilicus in neonates, injection sites and the feet. NEONATAL TETANUS presents in the FIRST 3-14 DAYS OF LIFE with a baby who fed and cried normally for the first two days and then develops INABILITY TO SUCK, excessive crying, stiffness, spasms and opisthotonus. Classify by the ABLETT grading of severity. DIFFERENTIAL DIAGNOSIS to exclude: dental abscess and other causes of trismus, strychnine poisoning (in which there is complete relaxation between spasms), dystonic reactions to metoclopramide, prochlorperazine and antipsychotics (which respond dramatically to an anticholinergic), meningitis, encephalitis, rabies, hypocalcaemic tetany and stiff-person syndrome

redFlags: TETANUS IS A MEDICAL EMERGENCY WITH HIGH MORTALITY AND REQUIRES IMMEDIATE ADMISSION, PREFERABLY TO INTENSIVE CARE - do not manage it in a general ward. IMMEDIATE PRIORITIES: secure the AIRWAY, since LARYNGEAL SPASM AND RESPIRATORY MUSCLE SPASM CAUSE SUDDEN ASPHYXIA AND ARE A LEADING CAUSE OF EARLY DEATH - have intubation and tracheostomy facilities immediately available and consider early elective tracheostomy
nurse in a QUIET, DARKENED ROOM WITH MINIMAL HANDLING AND STIMULATION, and cluster nursing interventions
give HUMAN TETANUS IMMUNOGLOBULIN as soon as possible to neutralise unbound toxin (bound toxin cannot be neutralised, so give it early)
DEBRIDE AND CLEAN THE WOUND thoroughly AFTER giving immunoglobulin
give METRONIDAZOLE as the antibiotic of choice
CONTROL SPASMS with benzodiazepines in high dose, escalating to magnesium sulphate, and to neuromuscular blockade with mechanical ventilation in severe cases
manage AUTONOMIC INSTABILITY with magnesium sulphate and short-acting agents, avoiding abrupt changes
provide nutritional support, thromboprophylaxis, pressure-area care and physiotherapy

watch for aspiration pneumonia, rhabdomyolysis, vertebral fractures from severe spasms, and sepsis. CRITICALLY, HAVING TETANUS DOES NOT CONFER IMMUNITY - THE TOXIN DOSE IS TOO SMALL TO IMMUNISE - so EVERY SURVIVOR MUST COMPLETE A FULL PRIMARY VACCINATION COURSE before discharge. PREVENTION IS EVERYTHING: ensure routine childhood immunisation and 10-yearly boosters

assess EVERY WOUND for tetanus-proneness (contamination with soil, dust or manure, puncture wounds, devitalised tissue, burns, frostbite, delay in treatment beyond 6 hours) and give vaccine and, where indicated, immunoglobulin

and prevent NEONATAL TETANUS through maternal immunisation in pregnancy and CLEAN DELIVERY AND CORD CARE PRACTICES - never apply cow dung, ash or other traditional substances to the cord stump. Tetanus is NOTIFIABLE

symptoms.sourceText: A generalised, intensely itchy vesicular rash appearing in successive crops, so that macules, papules, vesicles, pustules and crusts are all present simultaneously in the same area ('crops of different ages' - the cardinal diagnostic feature)
A brief prodrome of fever, headache, malaise, anorexia and myalgia for 1-2 days before the rash, which is more pronounced in adolescents and adults

The rash begins on the trunk, face and scalp and spreads centrifugally to the limbs, with a centripetal (central) distribution that is denser on the trunk than the extremities - the opposite of smallpox
Lesions appear on mucous membranes including the mouth, palate, conjunctiva and genitalia, where they ulcerate and cause soreness and dysphagia
Severe itching leading to scratching and secondary infection
Scabs separate after 1-2 weeks leaving hypopigmented marks and occasional pitted scars
Adults, adolescents, pregnant women, neonates, smokers and the immunocompromised have far more severe disease
Spread is by airborne droplet nuclei and by direct contact with vesicle fluid, with an attack rate over 90% in susceptible household contacts
Infectivity runs from 1-2 days before the rash until all lesions have crusted, usually about 5 days
The virus then remains latent in dorsal root ganglia and reactivates years later as herpes zoster

symptoms.masterName: Burning and itching of the eyes

signs: Fever of 38-39C

the RASH consists of lesions in ALL STAGES OF EVOLUTION IN THE SAME BODY AREA - erythematous macules progressing within hours to papules, then to the characteristic thin-walled clear vesicle on an erythematous base ('DEWDROP ON A ROSE PETAL'), which becomes pustular, umbilicated and then crusts
the distribution is CENTRIPETAL, concentrated on the trunk, face and scalp with relative sparing of the distal limbs
SCALP AND MUCOSAL INVOLVEMENT ARE CHARACTERISTIC AND HELP DISTINGUISH IT from other vesicular eruptions
excoriations and secondarily infected lesions with surrounding cellulitis, purulence and crusting
mild generalised lymphadenopathy
examine the chest for signs of VARICELLA PNEUMONIA (tachypnoea, crackles, hypoxia), which is much commoner in adults and smokers and may be present with surprisingly few auscultatory findings
assess for neurological signs of cerebellitis (ataxia, nystagmus) or encephalitis. DIAGNOSIS IS USUALLY CLINICAL

confirm where necessary by PCR of vesicle fluid or a swab of the lesion base (the most sensitive test), direct fluorescent antibody, or Tzanck smear showing multinucleated giant cells (which does not distinguish VZV from HSV)
VZV IgM and IgG serology assist in determining susceptibility, particularly in pregnancy and healthcare workers

redFlags: REFER OR ADMIT URGENTLY: VARICELLA PNEUMONIA - cough, breathlessness, tachypnoea, pleuritic pain and hypoxia appearing 1-6 days after the rash, which is the commonest serious complication in adults, is far more frequent and severe in SMOKERS AND IN PREGNANCY, and carries significant mortality (needs intravenous aciclovir and oxygen)
ENCEPHALITIS with headache, confusion, seizures and coma, or the milder ACUTE CEREBELLAR ATAXIA with unsteady gait and nystagmus in children

SEVERE SECONDARY BACTERIAL INFECTION with Staphylococcus aureus or group A Streptococcus, which can produce cellulitis, abscess, NECROTISING FASCIITIS, toxic shock syndrome, osteomyelitis and sepsis - suspect it if fever persists or recurs after the fourth day or if a lesion becomes intensely painful, indurated or spreading
HAEMORRHAGIC VARICELLA with bleeding into lesions
PURPURA FULMINANS
hepatitis
nephritis
thrombocytopenia

and stroke from VZV vasculopathy. SPECIAL SITUATIONS: PREGNANCY - varicella in the mother carries a high risk of severe pneumonia, and infection in the FIRST 20 WEEKS can cause CONGENITAL VARICELLA SYNDROME with limb hypoplasia, cicatricial skin scarring, eye and brain defects, while maternal infection FROM 5 DAYS BEFORE TO 2 DAYS AFTER DELIVERY causes severe NEONATAL VARICELLA with mortality up to 30% - such neonates need varicella-zoster immunoglobulin and aciclovir

the IMMUNOCOMPROMISED, including those on corticosteroids, chemotherapy or biologics and those with HIV, develop progressive disseminated varicella with visceral involvement and require immediate intravenous aciclovir
NEONATES and adults generally warrant antiviral therapy. PUBLIC HEALTH: isolate until all lesions have crusted
exclude from school and work
keep the patient away from pregnant women, neonates and immunocompromised individuals
offer POST-EXPOSURE PROPHYLAXIS with vaccine within 3-5 days to susceptible immunocompetent contacts, or VZIG (or aciclovir) to pregnant, neonatal and immunocompromised contacts
AVOID NSAIDs, particularly ibuprofen, because of an association with necrotising soft tissue infection, and AVOID ASPIRIN IN CHILDREN because of REYE SYNDROME
treat itch with calamine, antihistamines and cool baths, and keep nails short
conditions.firstLine: Acyclovir (800 mg by mouth five times daily) is recommended for adolescents and adults with chickenpox of 24 h in duration.

symptoms.sourceText: Fever above 38C with cough and rapidly progressive shortness of breath
Headache - in a person with recent exposure to poultry, sick or dead birds, live bird markets, or a confirmed human case, or who lives in or has travelled from an affected area
The illness characteristically progresses to severe pneumonia and respiratory failure within days
Diarrhoea, vomiting and abdominal pain, which are notably more frequent in H5N1 than in seasonal influenza and may be the presenting features
Conjunctivitis, which is characteristic of H7 subtypes (H7N7, H7N9) and may be the only manifestation
Encephalitis with seizures and altered consciousness has been described
The incubation period is typically 2-5 days but may extend to 7-10 days, longer than for seasonal influenza
The exposure history is the single most important diagnostic clue, since the clinical picture otherwise resembles severe community-acquired pneumonia

Human-to-human transmission has so far been limited and non-sustained, but any cluster of cases, or infection in a healthcare worker, is of extreme public health importance because of the pandemic potential of reassortment

redFlags: TREAT AS A PUBLIC HEALTH EMERGENCY AND NOTIFY IMMEDIATELY - any suspected case of avian influenza is IMMEDIATELY NOTIFIABLE to national authorities and WHO under the International Health Regulations, and must be reported on clinical and epidemiological suspicion without waiting for confirmation. INFECTION CONTROL: isolate the patient in a single room, ideally with negative pressure, and use AIRBORNE, DROPLET AND CONTACT PRECAUTIONS with an N95/FFP3 respirator, eye protection, gown and gloves for all staff, with particular care during aerosol-generating procedures. TREATMENT: START OSELTAMIVIR IMMEDIATELY ON SUSPICION WITHOUT WAITING FOR LABORATORY CONFIRMATION, since benefit depends on early administration
higher doses and longer courses are often used in severe disease
monitor for antiviral resistance
CORTICOSTEROIDS ARE NOT ROUTINELY RECOMMENDED and may be harmful
provide supportive care with oxygen, lung-protective ventilation and, where available, ECMO. CLINICAL RED FLAGS: rapidly progressive breathlessness or hypoxia
ARDS
multi-organ failure
septic shock
encephalitis or seizures
rhabdomyolysis
disseminated intravascular coagulation
and note that H5N1 CARRIES A CASE FATALITY OF ROUGHLY 50% IN REPORTED HUMAN CASES, with death typically from progressive respiratory failure.

CONTACT MANAGEMENT: identify, list and monitor all close and healthcare contacts for 7-10 days, offer post-exposure oseltamivir prophylaxis to high-risk contacts, and investigate any CLUSTER OF CASES OR HEALTHCARE-WORKER INFECTION URGENTLY, as this may signal the emergence of human-to-human transmission.

PREVENTION: avoid contact with sick or dead poultry and wild birds, avoid live bird markets in affected areas, cook poultry and eggs thoroughly, practise hand hygiene, ensure seasonal influenza vaccination of poultry workers to reduce the chance of reassortment, and support veterinary surveillance and culling

symptoms.sourceText: Pulmonary TB: cough for more than 2-3 weeks, initially dry and later productive of mucopurulent sputum
Evening rise of temperature with drenching night sweats
symptoms.masterName: Fever and malaise during an acute attack

symptoms.sourceText: These constitute the classical 'constitutional symptoms' and any adult with a cough of more than 2 weeks in an endemic area must be evaluated for tuberculosis

Extrapulmonary disease accounts for 15-20% of cases in the immunocompetent and far more in HIV - lymph node TB with painless, firm, matted cervical swellings that may soften, form a cold abscess and discharge through a sinus (scrofula)
Pleural TB with breathlessness, pleuritic pain and effusion
TB meningitis with 2-3 weeks of headache, low fever, vomiting, personality change, then cranial nerve palsies, confusion and coma
Spinal TB (POTT'S disease) with chronic back pain, local tenderness, gibbus deformity, paravertebral abscess and paraparesis
Abdominal TB with chronic pain, ascites, subacute obstruction and a 'doughy' abdomen
Renal TB with sterile pyuria and haematuria
Pericardial TB with breathlessness, oedema and constriction
Miliary TB with fever, weight loss and multi-organ involvement
TB of bones and joints, skin, adrenals and the female genital tract causing infertility

Risk factors - HIV (the single strongest), diabetes, malnutrition, silicosis, smoking, alcohol, corticosteroids, ANTI-TNF therapy, chronic kidney disease, transplantation, overcrowding, imprisonment and close contact with a case

signs: Cachexia and temporal wasting
low-grade fever
pallor
clubbing in chronic disease

CHEST examination is often surprisingly UNREMARKABLE relative to the radiographic extent, but may show reduced expansion, dullness, bronchial breathing, post-tussive crackles at the apices, amphoric breathing over a cavity, or the signs of pleural effusion or fibrosis with tracheal and mediastinal shift
LYMPHADENOPATHY - firm, matted, non-tender cervical nodes, sometimes with a discharging sinus
hepatosplenomegaly
ascites with a doughy feel
spinal tenderness and gibbus
neck stiffness, cranial nerve palsies (especially the sixth) and papilloedema in meningitis

choroidal tubercles on FUNDOSCOPY in miliary disease (pathognomonic). INVESTIGATIONS: SPUTUM for AFB smear microscopy (two specimens, at least one early morning) and, PREFERENTIALLY, RAPID MOLECULAR TESTING WITH XPERT MTB/RIF ULTRA AS THE INITIAL DIAGNOSTIC TEST IN ALL PRESUMPTIVE CASES, since it detects M. tuberculosis and RIFAMPICIN RESISTANCE WITHIN 2 HOURS with far greater sensitivity than smear
MYCOBACTERIAL CULTURE ON SOLID OR LIQUID MEDIA REMAINS THE GOLD STANDARD and provides full drug susceptibility testing, but takes 2-8 weeks

CHEST RADIOGRAPH classically shows upper lobe and apical infiltrates, CAVITATION, fibrosis, volume loss and hilar lymphadenopathy in adults (primary disease in children shows hilar nodes with a Ghon focus), and a fine reticulonodular 'MILLET SEED' pattern in miliary TB

for extrapulmonary disease obtain tissue or fluid for histology (CASEATING GRANULOMAS with Langhans giant cells), AFB stain, Xpert and culture, with a high ADENOSINE DEAMINASE level supporting TB in pleural, pericardial, peritoneal and CSF fluid, and CSF in TB meningitis showing lymphocytic pleocytosis with HIGH PROTEIN AND LOW GLUCOSE

TEST EVERY TB PATIENT FOR HIV, and screen for diabetes

redFlags: REFER OR ACT URGENTLY: massive HAEMOPTYSIS (may be fatal - resuscitate, protect the airway, position the bleeding side down and arrange bronchial artery embolisation)
TB MENINGITIS - a neurological emergency in which treatment must begin on clinical suspicion without waiting for confirmation, with ADJUNCTIVE CORTICOSTEROIDS, which reduce mortality
MILIARY TB
PERICARDIAL EFFUSION WITH TAMPONADE (raised JVP, pulsus paradoxus, muffled sounds)
SPINAL TB WITH NEUROLOGICAL DEFICIT OR CORD COMPRESSION (urgent surgical and neurological assessment)
tense ascites or intestinal obstruction
respiratory failure
pneumothorax

severe malnutrition. DRUG-RESISTANT TB IS A MAJOR RED FLAG - suspect MULTIDRUG-RESISTANT TB (resistant to isoniazid and rifampicin) in any patient who has been previously treated, has failed treatment, has relapsed or defaulted, is a contact of a known MDR case, or is not improving after 2-3 months of appropriate therapy: obtain rapid molecular resistance testing and refer to a specialist programme, as treatment requires prolonged multi-drug regimens. TREATMENT AND MONITORING: use standard regimens (typically 2 months of HRZE followed by 4 months of HR) with DIRECTLY OBSERVED OR SUPPORTED THERAPY, and stress that TREATMENT MUST BE COMPLETED IN FULL, since irregular or partial treatment is the principal driver of drug resistance

monitor for hepatotoxicity (nausea, vomiting, jaundice, abdominal pain - STOP the drugs and check liver function), isoniazid-related PERIPHERAL NEUROPATHY (PREVENT WITH PYRIDOXINE in all at-risk patients), ethambutol-induced OPTIC NEURITIS (warn about visual blurring and colour vision change and check acuity), rifampicin-induced orange discoloration of secretions and its major DRUG INTERACTIONS INCLUDING REDUCED EFFICACY OF ORAL CONTRACEPTIVES AND ANTIRETROVIRALS, and streptomycin ototoxicity and nephrotoxicity. PUBLIC HEALTH: TB IS NOTIFIABLE - report every case, screen all household and close contacts (especially children under 5 and people with HIV) and offer TB PREVENTIVE THERAPY where indicated, ensure infection control with respiratory isolation for smear-positive pulmonary cases and N95 respirators for staff, ventilation and cough hygiene, and provide nutritional and social support
conditions.firstLine: A combination of drugs is used for the treatment of TB disease (Table 186-2). For drugsusceptible disease, a standardized regimen is used with an intensive phase consisting of four drugs--isoniazid (H), rifampin (R), pyrazinamide (Z), and ethambutol (E)--given for 2 months, which is followed by a continuation phase of isoniazid and rifampin for 4 months, for a total treatment duration of 6 months.

symptoms.sourceText: Men: purulent or mucopurulent urethral discharge, typically profuse and creamy-yellow, appearing 2-5 days after exposure, with dysuria and urethral itching. women: often asymptomatic (up to 50-80%), or with increased vaginal discharge, dysuria, intermenstrual or postcoital bleeding and lower abdominal pain
Pharyngeal infection, usually asymptomatic but occasionally causing sore throat
Rectal infection with anal discharge, pruritus, tenesmus, painful defecation and bleeding, again often asymptomatic
Deep dyspareunia and pelvic pain in ascending infection
Conjunctivitis with copious purulent discharge in adults after autoinoculation and in neonates as ophthalmia neonatorum within the first 5 days of life
Fever, rash and joint pain in disseminated disease

Risk factors - new or multiple sexual partners, unprotected intercourse, a partner with symptoms, previous sexually transmitted infection, transactional sex, men who have sex with men, and adolescence
Note that coinfection with chlamydia trachomatis is present in A large proportion and must be treated concurrently
Acute urethritis is the most common presentation in men

signs: MEN: purulent yellow-green urethral discharge, expressible on milking the urethra, with a red oedematous meatus
tender swollen epididymis in epididymo-orchitis
a tender fluctuant swelling along the penile shaft (periurethral abscess)
inguinal lymphadenopathy. WOMEN: mucopurulent endocervical discharge with a FRIABLE CERVIX THAT BLEEDS EASILY ON CONTACT with a swab
vaginal wall erythema

in PELVIC INFLAMMATORY DISEASE, lower abdominal tenderness with CERVICAL MOTION TENDERNESS and adnexal tenderness, and right upper quadrant tenderness with a hepatic friction rub in FITZ-HUGH-CURTIS perihepatitis

Bartholin gland abscess. DISSEMINATED GONOCOCCAL INFECTION shows the classical triad of MIGRATORY POLYARTHRALGIA, TENOSYNOVITIS (typically of the wrists, hands and ankles) and a SPARSE PUSTULAR OR HAEMORRHAGIC-PUSTULAR RASH on the distal extremities, or alternatively a purulent monoarthritis of the knee. LABORATORY: GRAM STAIN of a male urethral smear showing GRAM-NEGATIVE INTRACELLULAR DIPLOCOCCI within polymorphs is highly sensitive and specific in symptomatic men, but is INSENSITIVE FOR CERVICAL, PHARYNGEAL AND RECTAL SPECIMENS
NUCLEIC ACID AMPLIFICATION TESTING (NAAT) IS THE INVESTIGATION OF CHOICE for all sites, including self-collected vaginal swabs and first-void urine
ALWAYS ALSO TAKE A CULTURE ON SELECTIVE MEDIUM (Thayer-Martin) BEFORE TREATMENT WHEREVER POSSIBLE, because culture is the only way to obtain ANTIMICROBIAL SUSCEPTIBILITY, which is now essential
SCREEN FOR CHLAMYDIA, SYPHILIS, HIV AND HEPATITIS B IN EVERY CASE, and take a full sexual history including all exposed sites

redFlags: OPHTHALMIA NEONATORUM - purulent conjunctivitis in a neonate in the first days of life is a SIGHT-THREATENING EMERGENCY, since gonococcus can penetrate an intact cornea and cause perforation and blindness within 24-48 hours: admit, take urgent swabs, give systemic third-generation cephalosporin and frequent saline irrigation, and treat the mother and her partner

ensure universal neonatal eye prophylaxis. DISSEMINATED GONOCOCCAL INFECTION with septic arthritis, and the rare but devastating gonococcal ENDOCARDITIS and MENINGITIS, require admission and intravenous therapy. Also urgent: PELVIC INFLAMMATORY DISEASE with fever and adnexal tenderness (treat immediately to preserve fertility, and always exclude ECTOPIC PREGNANCY with a pregnancy test)
tubo-ovarian abscess
epididymo-orchitis in a young man (EXCLUDE TESTICULAR TORSION, a surgical emergency)
gonococcal conjunctivitis in an adult
infection in PREGNANCY (risk of preterm labour, chorioamnionitis and neonatal transmission)

and GONOCOCCAL INFECTION IN A CHILD BEYOND THE NEONATAL PERIOD, WHICH IS EVIDENCE OF SEXUAL ABUSE UNTIL PROVEN OTHERWISE AND MANDATES SAFEGUARDING REFERRAL. ANTIMICROBIAL RESISTANCE IS THE OVERRIDING CONCERN - Neisseria gonorrhoeae has developed resistance to sulphonamides, penicillins, tetracyclines, fluoroquinolones and now increasingly to cephalosporins and azithromycin, and WHO lists it as a high-priority pathogen: use only current locally recommended first-line regimens (presently high-dose intramuscular CEFTRIAXONE), NEVER use fluoroquinolones empirically, obtain culture and susceptibility, and ARRANGE TEST-OF-CURE, particularly for pharyngeal infection and after any treatment failure. Additionally: notify and treat ALL SEXUAL PARTNERS from the preceding 60 days (or the most recent partner if longer), advise ABSTINENCE FOR 7 DAYS AFTER TREATMENT AND UNTIL PARTNERS ARE TREATED, treat presumptively for chlamydia, offer HIV testing and PrEP counselling, and report as required

symptoms.sourceText: Severe, sharp, KNIFE-LIKE or tearing pain during defecation, often described as 'passing broken glass', followed by a deep burning or throbbing ache that persists for minutes to several hours afterwards
Bright red bleeding, typically streaking the surface of the stool or seen on the toilet paper rather than mixed into the stool

Constipation, which is both the principal cause and the consequence, since the patient deliberately avoids defecation for fear of the pain, allowing the stool to harden further and perpetuating a vicious cycle
A palpable skin tag (sentinel pile) at the anal verge in chronic disease

Precipitants - passage of a hard constipated stool (the commonest), chronic diarrhoea, childbirth and vaginal delivery, anal intercourse, low-fibre diet, dehydration, opioid analgesics, and prolonged straining

The natural history distinguishes acute fissures of less than 6 weeks, which usually heal with conservative measures, from chronic fissures persisting beyond 6 weeks with characteristic secondary changes

signs: INSPECTION WITH GENTLE PARTING OF THE BUTTOCKS IS USUALLY DIAGNOSTIC AND IS ALL THAT IS REQUIRED - a longitudinal, linear or pear-shaped ulcer in the ANODERM. OVER 90% ARE LOCATED IN THE POSTERIOR MIDLINE, with about 10% anterior (commoner in women after childbirth). An ACUTE fissure appears as a fresh, sharply demarcated superficial tear with clean edges. A CHRONIC fissure shows the triad of INDURATED EVERTED EDGES with the exposed WHITE HORIZONTAL FIBRES OF THE INTERNAL ANAL SPHINCTER VISIBLE IN THE BASE, a SENTINEL SKIN TAG at the distal (external) end, and a HYPERTROPHIED ANAL PAPILLA at the proximal (internal) end. There is marked internal sphincter HYPERTONIA AND SPASM, which is central to the pathophysiology - the raised resting anal pressure causes ischaemia of the posterior commissure, which is the least well perfused part of the anal canal, and prevents healing. DIGITAL RECTAL EXAMINATION AND PROCTOSCOPY ARE EXTREMELY PAINFUL AND SHOULD BE DEFERRED in a typical acute fissure until the pain has settled or examination is performed under anaesthesia
do not force them. Note that a fissure that is LATERAL in position, MULTIPLE, IRREGULAR, PAINLESS, BROAD-BASED OR UNDERMINED IS ATYPICAL and demands investigation for an underlying cause

redFlags: ATYPICAL FISSURES REQUIRE URGENT INVESTIGATION AND REFERRAL - a fissure that is LATERALLY SITED, MULTIPLE, PAINLESS, IRREGULAR OR NON-HEALING should raise suspicion of CROHN'S DISEASE (look for perianal skin tags, fistulae, abscesses, diarrhoea, weight loss and mouth ulcers), TUBERCULOSIS, SYPHILIS (a painless indurated chancre), HERPES SIMPLEX, HIV-related ulceration, CHLAMYDIAL LYMPHOGRANULOMA VENEREUM, LEUKAEMIA, or ANAL CARCINOMA - and any suspicious ulcer must be BIOPSIED. Also refer: bleeding that is dark, mixed with the stool, or accompanied by a change in bowel habit, weight loss, anaemia, a family history of colorectal cancer or age over 45-50 (COLONOSCOPY to exclude colorectal malignancy - never attribute rectal bleeding to a fissure without careful assessment)
a perianal lump with severe throbbing pain, fever and fluctuance (PERIANAL OR ISCHIORECTAL ABSCESS, which requires urgent incision and drainage, and never resolves with antibiotics alone)
a fistula-in-ano with persistent discharge

severe pain with fever and extensive perineal swelling, crepitus or necrosis, particularly in a diabetic or immunocompromised patient (FOURNIER'S GANGRENE - a life-threatening surgical emergency requiring immediate debridement)
failure of an appropriately treated fissure to heal within 6-8 weeks
and recurrent fissures

symptoms.sourceText: A continuous, HIGH-PITCHED, musical whistling sound produced by airflow through narrowed intrathoracic airways, heard predominantly in expiration
Difficulty in breathing out with a prolonged expiratory phase
Audible whistling that may be heard by the patient or family without a stethoscope
Symptoms provoked by exercise, cold air, allergens, dust, smoke, strong smells, respiratory infection, aspirin or NSAIDs and beta blockers
Orthopnoea and paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnoea in cardiac causes ('cardiac asthma')
A history of choking or a sudden episode while eating or playing in a child (foreign body)
A personal or family history of atopy, asthma, eczema or hay fever
Symptoms can occur in relation to triggers but may also occur spontaneously

signs: First establish that the sound is truly wheeze and not STRIDOR, which is a harsh predominantly INSPIRATORY sound loudest over the NECK indicating EXTRATHORACIC UPPER AIRWAY obstruction and is a far more urgent finding. GENERALISED, BILATERAL, POLYPHONIC EXPIRATORY WHEEZE with a prolonged expiratory phase indicates diffuse small airway narrowing as in asthma and COPD. A FIXED, LOCALISED, MONOPHONIC WHEEZE THAT DOES NOT CLEAR WITH COUGHING INDICATES OBSTRUCTION OF A SINGLE LARGE AIRWAY and must be investigated for TUMOUR, FOREIGN BODY, or extrinsic compression by node or mass. Assess: respiratory rate, ability to speak in full sentences, use of ACCESSORY MUSCLES, intercostal, subcostal and suprasternal RECESSION, tracheal tug, nasal flaring and grunting in children, cyanosis, level of consciousness, pulse rate, PULSUS PARADOXUS, OXYGEN SATURATION and PEAK EXPIRATORY FLOW RATE
hyperinflation with a barrel chest, hyperresonance and reduced breath sounds
look for raised JVP, basal crackles, a third heart sound, displaced apex and pedal oedema (cardiac failure)
urticaria, angioedema and hypotension (anaphylaxis)
clubbing and copious sputum (bronchiectasis)

lymphadenopathy and weight loss (malignancy). INVESTIGATIONS: spirometry with bronchodilator reversibility, peak flow charting, chest radiography (essential for a localised wheeze, suspected foreign body or first presentation in an older adult), full blood count with EOSINOPHIL COUNT, IgE and, where relevant, filarial serology
ECG and BNP or echocardiography if a cardiac cause is possible
and bronchoscopy for a persistent localised wheeze
Wheeze may be persistent

redFlags: TREAT AS AN EMERGENCY: SILENT CHEST - the disappearance of wheeze in a distressed, exhausted patient indicates that airflow is now too poor to generate sound and is an OMINOUS SIGN OF LIFE-THREATENING AIRWAY OBSTRUCTION, NOT IMPROVEMENT
cyanosis
exhaustion, confusion or drowsiness
inability to speak more than single words
SpO2 below 92%
PEFR below 33-50% of predicted
bradycardia or hypotension

a rising or normal PaCO2 in an acutely breathless asthmatic (indicating fatigue and impending respiratory arrest). ANAPHYLAXIS - wheeze with urticaria, angioedema, hypotension or collapse after an allergen, sting, food or drug requires IMMEDIATE INTRAMUSCULAR ADRENALINE, not bronchodilators alone. STRIDOR AT REST, drooling, muffled voice or inability to swallow indicates UPPER AIRWAY OBSTRUCTION (epiglottitis, croup, foreign body, angioedema) and requires urgent airway assessment - DO NOT EXAMINE THE THROAT OR DISTRESS THE CHILD. SUDDEN-ONSET UNILATERAL WHEEZE IN A CHILD, especially with a history of choking, is a FOREIGN BODY until proven otherwise and needs urgent bronchoscopy (a normal chest radiograph does not exclude it - ask for expiratory or decubitus films showing air trapping). ACUTE PULMONARY OEDEMA presenting as wheeze in an older patient with orthopnoea, raised JVP and crackles must not be treated as asthma. Other red flags: wheeze with fever and focal signs (pneumonia)
wheeze with pleuritic pain, haemoptysis and tachycardia (pulmonary embolism)
new wheeze in a smoker over 40 with weight loss or haemoptysis (bronchial carcinoma)
persistent localised monophonic wheeze
failure to respond to bronchodilators
recurrent wheeze in an infant with poor growth (cystic fibrosis, immunodeficiency, congenital anomaly, tracheo-oesophageal fistula)
and marked EOSINOPHILIA with nocturnal wheeze in an endemic area (tropical pulmonary eosinophilia, which responds to diethylcarbamazine)
conditions.firstLine: supportive care - use of bronchodilators for relief of wheezing during asthmatic episodes

source.guideline: Harrison's 21e Ch.37 (Dyspnea) and Ch.287 (Asthma); Robbins & Cotran 10e Ch.15; WHO ICD-11 MD11.7

symptoms.sourceText: An elevation of body temperature above the normal daily variation - conventionally an oral temperature above 37.8C (100F), a rectal or core temperature above 38.0C (100.4F), or an axillary temperature above 37.2C
Feeling hot or, paradoxically, cold during the rising phase
In children, irritability, poor feeding, drowsiness and febrile convulsions between 6 months and 5 years
Delirium and confusion, especially in the elderly and in high fever

The pattern and associated features direct the diagnosis - a continuous fever with a stepladder rise (typhoid), an intermittent fever with paroxysms every 48 or 72 hours (malaria), an undulant fever (brucellosis), an evening rise with night sweats and weight loss (tuberculosis), a remittent fever with rigors (abscess or pyogenic infection), and a Pel-Ebstein pattern (Hodgkin lymphoma)

Always elicit localising symptoms - cough, dysuria, diarrhoea, headache with neck stiffness, ear pain, sore throat, rash, joint pain, abdominal pain - as well as travel history, animal and insect exposure, sick contacts, immunisation status, drug history including recent antibiotics and any new medication (drug fever), recent surgery or instrumentation, indwelling devices, injecting drug use, immunosuppression and HIV status

signs: MEASURE THE TEMPERATURE ACCURATELY AND CONSISTENTLY BY ROUTE, and record the pulse, respiratory rate, blood pressure, oxygen saturation, capillary refill and level of consciousness. Look for RELATIVE BRADYCARDIA (typhoid, brucellosis, legionella, dengue) or disproportionate tachycardia. UNDERTAKE A SYSTEMATIC HEAD-TO-TOE SEARCH FOR A FOCUS: throat and tonsils, ears and mastoids, sinuses, teeth and gums
neck stiffness, Kernig and Brudzinski signs and the fundi for papilloedema
lymph nodes at all sites
chest for consolidation and effusion
heart for a NEW MURMUR, and for splinter haemorrhages, Osler nodes, Janeway lesions and Roth spots (INFECTIVE ENDOCARDITIS)
abdomen for tenderness, guarding, organomegaly and renal angle tenderness
SKIN FOR RASH - and in particular for a NON-BLANCHING PETECHIAL OR PURPURIC RASH, which demands immediate action
joints for effusion
calves for deep vein thrombosis
perineum, genitalia and rectum
all indwelling lines, catheters and surgical wounds

and pressure areas. INVESTIGATIONS guided by the assessment: full blood count with differential (neutrophilia in bacterial infection, LEUCOPENIA WITH LYMPHOCYTOSIS in typhoid, dengue and many viral infections, EOSINOPHILIA in parasitic and allergic disease), CRP and procalcitonin, blood cultures (at least two sets before antibiotics), urinalysis and culture, MALARIA THICK AND THIN FILMS OR RAPID TEST IN ANYONE WITH RELEVANT TRAVEL, chest radiograph, renal and liver function, dengue NS1 and serology, typhoid blood culture, HIV test, and further imaging, lumbar puncture, echocardiography or biopsy as indicated. FEVER OF UNKNOWN ORIGIN is defined as a temperature above 38.3C on several occasions for more than 3 weeks with no diagnosis after appropriate initial investigation, and its major causes are infection, malignancy (especially lymphoma and renal cell carcinoma), connective tissue and inflammatory disease, and drugs

tests.sourceText: throat and tonsils, ears and mastoids, sinuses, teeth and gums

full blood count with differential (neutrophilia in bacterial infection, LEUCOPENIA WITH LYMPHOCYTOSIS in typhoid, dengue and many viral infections, EOSINOPHILIA in parasitic and allergic disease), CRP and procalcitonin, blood cultures (at least two sets before antibiotics), urinalysis and culture, MALARIA THICK AND THIN FILMS OR RAPID TEST IN ANYONE WITH RELEVANT TRAVEL, chest radiograph, renal and liver function, dengue NS1 and serology, typhoid blood culture, HIV test, and further imaging, lumbar puncture, echocardiography or biopsy as indicated. FEVER OF UNKNOWN ORIGIN is defined as a temperature above 38.3C on several occasions for more than 3 weeks with no diagnosis after appropriate initial investigation, and its major causes are infection, malignancy (especially lymphoma and renal cell carcinoma), connective tissue and inflammatory disease, and drugs

redFlags: TREAT AS AN EMERGENCY: FEVER WITH A NON-BLANCHING PETECHIAL OR PURPURIC RASH (MENINGOCOCCAL SEPTICAEMIA - give parenteral antibiotics IMMEDIATELY and transfer, without waiting for investigations)
fever with neck stiffness, photophobia, altered consciousness or seizures (MENINGITIS or ENCEPHALITIS)

SEPSIS AND SEPTIC SHOCK - use a recognised screening tool and look for tachypnoea above 22/min, systolic BP below 100 mmHg, altered mentation, prolonged capillary refill, mottling, oliguria and a raised lactate, and deliver the SEPSIS SIX WITHIN ONE HOUR (oxygen, blood cultures, intravenous antibiotics, intravenous fluids, lactate and urine output monitoring)

FEVER IN A NEUTROPENIC PATIENT (a single temperature above 38.3C or 38.0C sustained for an hour in a patient on chemotherapy is FEBRILE NEUTROPENIA, a medical emergency requiring immediate broad-spectrum antibiotics within one hour and admission)

FEVER IN A RETURNING TRAVELLER FROM A MALARIA-ENDEMIC AREA (falciparum malaria until proven otherwise - do not delay films or treatment, and remember viral haemorrhagic fever in the appropriate epidemiological context, which requires isolation and specialist advice)
fever in an infant UNDER 3 MONTHS (a full septic screen and admission are usually required, as the presentation of serious bacterial infection is non-specific)

fever with any of the WHO/IMCI danger signs in a child - inability to drink or feed, vomiting everything, convulsions, lethargy or unconsciousness, stridor at rest, severe chest indrawing or severe malnutrition
fever with a new murmur or in a patient with prosthetic valves or intravascular devices (endocarditis - take three sets of blood cultures)
fever with severe unilateral joint pain and swelling (SEPTIC ARTHRITIS - aspirate urgently)
fever with right upper quadrant pain and jaundice (ascending cholangitis)
fever in an asplenic, immunosuppressed, transplant or HIV-positive patient
fever with focal neurological signs

hyperpyrexia above 41C, or fever with rigidity and altered consciousness on antipsychotics (neuroleptic malignant syndrome) or serotonergic drugs (serotonin syndrome), or after exertion in heat (HEAT STROKE, which requires active cooling rather than antipyretics)
conditions.firstLine: supportive care - ensure adequate hydration, provide antipyretics as needed.

source.guideline: Harrison's 21e Ch.19 (Fever) and Ch.21 (Fever of Unknown Origin); Robbins & Cotran 10e Ch.3 (Inflammation); WHO IMCI Guidelines; ICD-11 MG26

symptoms.sourceText: A new loss or alteration of the sense of smell (anosmia) or taste (ageusia), which is highly suggestive
Skin manifestations including a maculopapular or urticarial rash and 'covid toes' (pernio-like acral lesions)
Confusion, which may be the presenting feature in the elderly, along with falls, reduced mobility and functional decline without typical respiratory symptoms

The illness in most people is mild and self-limiting over 1-2 weeks, but a proportion deteriorate in the second week, typically around days 7-10, as the inflammatory phase supervenes - so the timing of presentation relative to symptom onset matters greatly

POST-COVID-19 condition (long covid) persisting beyond 12 weeks with fatigue, breathlessness, chest pain, palpitations, cognitive impairment or 'brain fog', sleep disturbance, POTS-like autonomic symptoms, anxiety and depression

Risk factors for severe disease - advancing age (the dominant factor), obesity, diabetes, hypertension, chronic cardiac, respiratory, renal or liver disease, immunosuppression, malignancy, pregnancy, and incomplete vaccination
Symptoms of gastrointestinal involvement (nausea and vomiting) and mental health consequences (depression, anxiety, sleep disturbances)

signs: Fever
TACHYPNOEA, which is an important early marker of deterioration
TACHYCARDIA

and, critically, HYPOXAEMIA MEASURED BY PULSE OXIMETRY - a resting SpO2 below 94% on air, or a fall of 3% or more on exertion, is a key trigger for escalation, and 'SILENT' OR HAPPY HYPOXIA, in which the patient is strikingly comfortable and not visibly distressed despite marked desaturation, is a well-described and dangerous phenomenon that makes OBJECTIVE OXIMETRY, INCLUDING AN EXERTIONAL DESATURATION TEST, ESSENTIAL RATHER THAN RELYING ON APPEARANCE. Chest auscultation may reveal bilateral basal crackles or be unremarkable
assess accessory muscle use, ability to complete sentences, cyanosis and level of consciousness

look for calf swelling and signs of venous thromboembolism, which is markedly increased in COVID-19. INVESTIGATIONS: confirm with RT-PCR on a nasopharyngeal or combined throat and nose swab, or a rapid antigen test (less sensitive, particularly in asymptomatic or late infection)
LYMPHOPENIA is characteristic and correlates with severity
raised CRP, ferritin, LDH and D-DIMER (a markedly raised D-dimer suggests thrombosis and predicts worse outcome)
deranged liver enzymes
raised troponin in cardiac involvement
CHEST RADIOGRAPH showing bilateral peripheral and lower zone infiltrates, and CT showing BILATERAL PERIPHERAL GROUND-GLASS OPACIFICATION with or without consolidation and a crazy-paving pattern
blood gases in the unwell

Chest auscultation may reveal bilateral basal crackles or be unremarkable

raised CRP, ferritin, LDH and D-DIMER (a markedly raised D-dimer suggests thrombosis and predicts worse outcome)
CHEST RADIOGRAPH showing bilateral peripheral and lower zone infiltrates, and CT showing BILATERAL PERIPHERAL GROUND-GLASS OPACIFICATION with or without consolidation and a crazy-paving pattern
monitor renal function and electrolyte levels, particularly in patients receiving remdesivir

redFlags: REFER OR ADMIT URGENTLY: SpO2 BELOW 92-94% ON AIR OR A SIGNIFICANT DROP ON EXERTION
RESPIRATORY RATE ABOVE 24-30/min
severe breathlessness or inability to complete a sentence
cyanosis
confusion, drowsiness or a new inability to perform usual activities
hypotension or signs of shock
reduced urine output
chest pain (myocarditis, pulmonary embolism or acute coronary syndrome)
haemoptysis
clinical deterioration around days 7-10, which is the classic timing of the inflammatory phase

and any patient at high risk who is symptomatic and may be eligible for EARLY ANTIVIRAL THERAPY (nirmatrelvir-ritonavir, remdesivir) OR MONOCLONAL ANTIBODIES, WHICH MUST BE GIVEN WITHIN THE FIRST FEW DAYS OF SYMPTOM ONSET TO BE EFFECTIVE - so identify and refer these patients promptly rather than waiting for deterioration. Specific complications to watch for: THROMBOEMBOLISM, with a substantially raised risk of pulmonary embolism, deep vein thrombosis and stroke, warranting thromboprophylaxis in admitted patients and a low threshold for imaging
myocarditis and arrhythmia

secondary bacterial and fungal infection, including COVID-ASSOCIATED PULMONARY ASPERGILLOSIS and, in settings with poorly controlled diabetes and heavy steroid use, RHINO-ORBITAL MUCORMYCOSIS presenting with facial pain, nasal blockage, black eschar on the palate or turbinate, periorbital swelling and ophthalmoplegia - a surgical emergency
acute kidney injury
diabetic ketoacidosis and steroid-induced hyperglycaemia

and in children, MULTISYSTEM INFLAMMATORY SYNDROME (MIS-C/PIMS-TS) presenting weeks after infection with persistent fever, rash, conjunctivitis, abdominal pain, hypotension and cardiac dysfunction, which requires urgent paediatric admission.
conditions.firstLine: supportive care - provide supplemental oxygen to maintain SpO2 92-96%, consider awake proning, and escalate to high-flow oxygen, CPAP or ventilation as needed.

rx.titration: Renal function should be monitored and dosing adjusted as necessary.
rx.renalAdjust: Adjust dosage in cases of renal impairment.

symptoms.sourceText: A persistent, subjective sense of tiredness, exhaustion or lack of energy that is not relieved by rest and is disproportionate to exertion
Reduced capacity for physical and mental work
A need for prolonged rest after activity
symptoms.masterName: A need for prolonged rest after activity

symptoms.sourceText: Generalised weakness (which must be distinguished from true muscle weakness, a neurological sign)
POST-EXERTIONAL malaise with symptoms worsening for more than 24 hours after activity (characteristic of myalgic encephalomyelitis/chronic fatigue syndrome)
The associated features direct the diagnosis - breathlessness and pallor (anaemia)
Weight loss, night sweats and fever (malignancy, tuberculosis, HIV)
Cold intolerance, constipation, weight gain and dry skin (hypothyroidism)
Heat intolerance, palpitations and weight loss (thyrotoxicosis)
Low mood, anhedonia, early morning wakening and guilt (depression)
Snoring, witnessed apnoeas and morning headache (obstructive sleep apnoea)
Postural dizziness, salt craving and pigmentation (adrenal insufficiency)
Joint pain, rash and photosensitivity (connective tissue disease)

A full drug history - beta blockers, antihistamines, sedatives, opioids, statins, antidepressants, antiepileptics, antihypertensives - and enquiry about alcohol, substance use, caffeine, shift work, carer responsibilities and psychosocial stress
Intense fatigue, cognitive dysfunction, and unrefreshing sleep (myalgic encephalomyelitis/chronic fatigue syndrome)

signs: GENERAL EXAMINATION IS DIRECTED AT FINDING AN ORGANIC CAUSE and may be entirely normal. Assess: weight, BMI and any documented weight change
PALLOR of the conjunctivae, palms and nail beds, with koilonychia and glossitis (iron deficiency)
jaundice
lymphadenopathy at all sites
thyroid for goitre, and for tremor, lid lag, bradycardia and a DELAYED RELAXATION OF THE ANKLE JERK
pulse, blood pressure LYING AND STANDING (postural drop in adrenal insufficiency and autonomic dysfunction)
hyperpigmentation of palmar creases, buccal mucosa and scars (Addison's disease)
cardiovascular examination for murmurs, heart failure and arrhythmia
respiratory examination
abdominal examination for organomegaly and masses

a full NEUROLOGICAL examination to distinguish fatigue from TRUE WEAKNESS - test power formally, look for fatigability on repeated effort and ptosis (MYASTHENIA GRAVIS), proximal weakness with difficulty rising from a chair (myopathy), and wasting and fasciculation
joints for synovitis
skin for rash

and a MENTAL STATE EXAMINATION with formal screening for depression and anxiety using PHQ-9 and GAD-7, and for sleep disorder using the Epworth Sleepiness Scale and STOP-BANG. A REASONABLE FIRST-LINE INVESTIGATION PANEL comprises: full blood count, ESR and CRP, ferritin and iron studies, renal function and electrolytes, calcium, liver function, glucose and HbA1c, THYROID FUNCTION, vitamin B12 and folate, VITAMIN D, COELIAC SEROLOGY, creatine kinase, urinalysis, HIV test where relevant, chest radiograph if indicated, and in women of reproductive age a pregnancy test

tests.sourceText: full blood count, ESR and CRP, ferritin and iron studies, renal function and electrolytes, calcium, liver function, glucose and HbA1c, THYROID FUNCTION, vitamin B12 and folate, VITAMIN D, COELIAC SEROLOGY, creatine kinase, urinalysis, HIV test where relevant, chest radiograph if indicated, and in women of reproductive age a pregnancy test

a full NEUROLOGICAL examination to distinguish fatigue from TRUE WEAKNESS - test power formally, look for fatigability on repeated effort and ptosis (MYASTHENIA GRAVIS), proximal weakness with difficulty rising from a chair (myopathy), and wasting and fasciculation
hyperpigmentation of palmar creases, buccal mucosa and scars (Addison's disease)

redFlags: RED FLAGS REQUIRING PROMPT INVESTIGATION: UNINTENTIONAL WEIGHT LOSS
FEVER, NIGHT SWEATS OR RIGORS
LYMPHADENOPATHY, particularly if firm, fixed, matted or supraclavicular
a palpable MASS anywhere
bone pain
unexplained BRUISING, BLEEDING OR PETECHIAE, or recurrent infections (haematological malignancy - check the full blood count and film urgently)
PALLOR with breathlessness or postural symptoms (significant anaemia - and any anaemia in a man or a postmenopausal woman requires investigation of the gastrointestinal tract for malignancy)
HAEMOPTYSIS, a persistent cough or a change in bowel habit

PROGRESSIVE BREATHLESSNESS OR CHEST PAIN (cardiac failure, ischaemic heart disease or arrhythmia - fatigue may be the sole presentation of heart failure and of myocardial infarction in the elderly and in diabetics)
confusion or focal neurological signs
TRUE MUSCLE WEAKNESS rather than subjective tiredness, especially if progressive, or with fatigable ptosis and diplopia (myasthenia gravis - beware of respiratory muscle involvement)
SUICIDAL IDEATION in a fatigued and depressed patient
fatigue with jaundice, ascites or oedema
fatigue in a patient with known malignancy or on chemotherapy

and fatigue lasting more than 6 months with post-exertional malaise, unrefreshing sleep and cognitive impairment, after organic causes have been excluded, which suggests MYALGIC ENCEPHALOMYELITIS/CHRONIC FATIGUE SYNDROME
referralCriteria: new onset of fatigue where organic cause has not been identified and ongoing investigations are required
patients with symptoms of myalgic encephalomyelitis/chronic fatigue syndrome for supportive treatment
severe fatigue associated with significant impairments of daily functioning that requires further management
conditions.firstLine: supportive care - activity management and cognitive-behavioral therapy.

rx.indication: treatment of chronic fatigue when symptoms of depression are present

evidenceRefs.note: antidepressants may improve fatigue in chronic fatigue syndrome.

rx.indication: improvement in fatigue associated with low vitamin D status
rx.renalAdjust: dose may need adjustment in renal impairment

evidenceRefs.note: Vitamin D replacement may improve fatigue.

symptoms.sourceText: Pain in the head, which may be described as throbbing, pressing, tightening, stabbing, boring or explosive
The characterisation depends on site, severity, quality, onset, duration, periodicity, aggravating and relieving factors and associated symptoms, which together identify the underlying disorder
Visual aura, scintillating scotoma or field loss

Lacrimation, conjunctival injection, nasal congestion, ptosis and miosis on the same side as the pain (cluster headache, in which the patient is restless and agitated, pacing about, in contrast to the migraineur who lies still)
Scalp tenderness on combing the hair, jaw claudication on chewing, and visual loss in a patient over 50 (giant cell arteritis)

Postural relationship - worse on standing and relieved by lying flat (low CSF pressure) or worse on lying flat, in the early morning, and on coughing, sneezing or straining, with vomiting (raised intracranial pressure)
Pulsatile tinnitus and transient visual obscurations in an obese young woman (idiopathic intracranial hypertension)
Eye pain with haloes, a red eye and vomiting (acute ANGLE-CLOSURE glaucoma)
Facial pain over the sinuses with purulent nasal discharge (sinusitis)
Analgesic use on 10-15 or more days a month (MEDICATION-OVERUSE headache)

The primary headache disorders - migraine, tension-type and the trigeminal autonomic cephalalgias - account for the great majority, but the essential clinical task is to identify the minority with secondary, dangerous causes

signs: A FULL NEUROLOGICAL EXAMINATION IS MANDATORY IN ANY NEW OR CHANGED HEADACHE. Check: level of consciousness and cognition
FUNDOSCOPY FOR PAPILLOEDEMA (and for spontaneous venous pulsation, whose presence argues against raised pressure)

visual acuity, VISUAL FIELDS BY CONFRONTATION (bitemporal hemianopia in a pituitary lesion), pupils and eye movements, looking for a THIRD NERVE PALSY WITH A DILATED PUPIL (posterior communicating artery aneurysm - a warning of impending subarachnoid haemorrhage) and a SIXTH NERVE PALSY (a false localising sign of raised intracranial pressure)
the remaining cranial nerves
limb power, tone, reflexes, plantar responses, coordination and gait
NECK STIFFNESS, Kernig's and Brudzinski's signs
PALPATE THE TEMPORAL ARTERIES for tenderness, thickening, nodularity and absent pulsation in anyone over 50
palpate the sinuses, temporomandibular joints and cervical spine
examine the EYES for a red eye, a hazy cornea, a fixed mid-dilated pupil and a stony-hard globe (acute angle-closure glaucoma)
check BLOOD PRESSURE

look for skin rash. INVESTIGATIONS ARE NOT REQUIRED IN A TYPICAL PRIMARY HEADACHE WITH A NORMAL EXAMINATION, but where indicated: URGENT NON-CONTRAST CT for thunderclap or suspected haemorrhage, followed by LUMBAR PUNCTURE AT 12 HOURS FOR XANTHOCHROMIA IF THE CT IS NEGATIVE (CT sensitivity falls with time)
MRI and MR/CT venography for suspected venous sinus thrombosis, posterior fossa lesions or low-pressure headache
ESR AND CRP URGENTLY IN SUSPECTED GIANT CELL ARTERITIS, with temporal artery ultrasound or biopsy
lumbar puncture with OPENING PRESSURE for meningitis and idiopathic intracranial hypertension
intraocular pressure measurement

ESR AND CRP URGENTLY IN SUSPECTED GIANT CELL ARTERITIS, with temporal artery ultrasound or biopsy

redFlags: THE RED FLAGS (SNNOOP10) DEMAND URGENT ACTION: SYSTEMIC symptoms including FEVER, or a rash, or neck stiffness (MENINGITIS or ENCEPHALITIS - give antibiotics and aciclovir without delay)
NEOPLASM in the history (metastasis)
NEUROLOGICAL DEFICIT, seizure, confusion or altered consciousness

ONSET THAT IS SUDDEN AND ABRUPT - a THUNDERCLAP HEADACHE REACHING MAXIMUM INTENSITY WITHIN ONE MINUTE, DESCRIBED AS THE WORST HEADACHE OF THE PATIENT'S LIFE, OFTEN WITH VOMITING, COLLAPSE OR NECK STIFFNESS, IS SUBARACHNOID HAEMORRHAGE UNTIL PROVEN OTHERWISE and requires immediate CT and, if negative, lumbar puncture
OLDER AGE OF ONSET, especially over 50 (giant cell arteritis, tumour)
PATTERN CHANGE or a progressive worsening headache
POSITIONAL headache
headache PRECIPITATED BY SNEEZING, COUGHING OR EXERCISE (posterior fossa lesion, Chiari malformation)
PAPILLOEDEMA
PROGRESSIVE headache with atypical features
PREGNANCY OR PUERPERIUM (cerebral venous sinus thrombosis, pre-eclampsia, pituitary apoplexy)
PAINFUL EYE with autonomic features
POST-TRAUMATIC onset (subdural or extradural haematoma - beware the lucid interval, and the elderly or anticoagulated patient with trivial trauma)
PAINKILLER OVERUSE

and PATIENTS WITH IMMUNE COMPROMISE OR HIV (toxoplasmosis, cryptococcal meningitis, lymphoma). Specific emergencies: GIANT CELL ARTERITIS - a new headache in a patient over 50 with scalp tenderness, jaw claudication, visual symptoms and a raised ESR REQUIRES IMMEDIATE HIGH-DOSE CORTICOSTEROIDS BEFORE BIOPSY, as delay causes irreversible blindness
ACUTE ANGLE-CLOSURE GLAUCOMA
CO POISONING in a household with multiple affected members and a faulty heater
hypertensive emergency
and pituitary apoplexy with sudden headache, ophthalmoplegia and visual loss
referralCriteria: Patients who do not have a clear diagnosis, have a primary headache disorder other than migraine or tension-type headache, or are unresponsive to two or more standard therapies for the considered headache type should be referred to a specialist.
conditions.firstLine: supportive care - NSAIDs for acute attack management in migraine.

symptoms.sourceText: Frequently asymptomatic or associated with only mild symptoms

The commonest presenting complaint is the passage of motile, flat, white, RIBBON-LIKE segments (proglottids) in the stool or spontaneously through the anus and onto clothing or bedding, which is highly distressing to the patient
Perianal itching and discomfort as proglottids migrate
Anxiety and disturbed sleep once the patient becomes aware of the worm

The species matter clinically - taenia saginata (the beef tapeworm), acquired by eating raw or undercooked beef containing cysticerci, grows up to 10 metres and its actively motile proglottids commonly crawl out of the anus spontaneously

Taenia solium (the pork tapeworm), acquired from raw or undercooked pork, is shorter at 2-8 metres and its proglottids are less motile, but it is far more dangerous because the human can also serve as the intermediate host, developing cysticercosis and neurocysticercosis after ingesting the eggs by the faeco-oral route from a carrier (including by autoinfection)
Taenia asiatica is acquired from pig viscera
Symptomatic manifestations may arise in some patients with heavy infections, including possible organ damage associated with cysticercosis

signs: Physical examination is usually entirely NORMAL

there may be mild abdominal tenderness, and in a minority some weight loss. DIAGNOSIS: examination of the STOOL and of PROGLOTTIDS is central - the SPECIES IS DISTINGUISHED BY COUNTING THE PRIMARY LATERAL UTERINE BRANCHES OF A GRAVID PROGLOTTID cleared or injected with India ink: TAENIA SAGINATA HAS 15-30 BRANCHES ON EACH SIDE, WHILE TAENIA SOLIUM HAS ONLY 7-13 - AND THIS DISTINCTION IS OF MAJOR CLINICAL IMPORTANCE, since T. solium carries the risk of cysticercosis for the patient and for household contacts. The SCOLEX also differs - T. saginata has four suckers and NO hooklets, whereas T. SOLIUM HAS FOUR SUCKERS AND A ROSTELLUM ARMED WITH A DOUBLE ROW OF HOOKLETS ('ARMED' TAPEWORM). THE EGGS OF THE TWO SPECIES ARE MORPHOLOGICALLY IDENTICAL - brown, spherical, 30-40 micrometres, with a thick radially striated shell containing a six-hooked oncosphere - SO EGGS ALONE CANNOT SPECIATE THE INFECTION
the perianal cellophane tape swab increases egg detection for T. saginata
stool PCR and coproantigen ELISA give species-specific diagnosis where available. Peripheral EOSINOPHILIA is mild or absent in intestinal taeniasis
check serology for cysticercosis where T. solium is identified or suspected
Perianal inspection may reveal irritation or inflammation
Abdominal tenderness may be noted upon palpation in some patients

tests.sourceText: the perianal cellophane tape swab increases egg detection for T. saginata
stool PCR and coproantigen ELISA give species-specific diagnosis where available. Peripheral EOSINOPHILIA is mild or absent in intestinal taeniasis
check serology for cysticercosis where T. solium is identified or suspected

redFlags: THE CRITICAL RED FLAG IS IDENTIFICATION OF TAENIA SOLIUM, BECAUSE OF THE RISK OF CYSTICERCOSIS AND NEUROCYSTICERCOSIS: a T. solium carrier is a danger to themselves and to their household, and every such case requires prompt treatment, careful hand and food hygiene education, and SCREENING OF HOUSEHOLD CONTACTS FOR BOTH TAENIASIS AND CYSTICERCOSIS. Refer or investigate urgently: NEW-ONSET SEIZURES, headache, focal neurological deficit or raised intracranial pressure in a person with taeniasis or from an endemic area (NEUROCYSTICERCOSIS - image the brain BEFORE treating, since anthelmintic-induced destruction of cysts provokes intense inflammation and can precipitate seizures, cerebral oedema and, with intraventricular cysts, acute hydrocephalus
treatment must be given with corticosteroid and anticonvulsant cover under specialist supervision)

visual disturbance or eye pain (OCULAR CYSTICERCOSIS - ALWAYS EXAMINE THE FUNDI AND EXCLUDE INTRAOCULAR CYSTS BEFORE GIVING ANTHELMINTICS, since inflammation around a dying intraocular cyst can destroy vision)
subcutaneous nodules

and in DIPHYLLOBOTHRIUM latum infection (the fish tapeworm, an important differential) MEGALOBLASTIC ANAEMIA FROM VITAMIN B12 DEFICIENCY. Other considerations: intestinal obstruction, appendicitis or biliary obstruction from migrating proglottids are rare but reported

PRAZIQUANTEL (single dose) OR NICLOSAMIDE is curative for intestinal taeniasis, and a purgative may be given to recover the scolex and confirm cure - note that PRAZIQUANTEL SHOULD BE USED WITH CAUTION IN A PATIENT WHO MAY HAVE NEUROCYSTICERCOSIS. PREVENTION AND PUBLIC HEALTH: taeniasis is preventable by THOROUGH COOKING OF BEEF AND PORK to at least 63C or freezing at -10C for several days, meat inspection and condemnation of infected carcasses, improved pig husbandry with confinement of pigs away from human faeces, SANITATION AND SAFE DISPOSAL OF HUMAN FAECES, hand washing, safe water and health education
T. solium is a WHO-listed neglected tropical disease targeted for control through combined human and porcine interventions

symptoms.sourceText: The manifestations depend entirely on the location of the cysts. neurocysticercosis, which is the most important form, presents most commonly with NEW-ONSET seizures (focal or generalised) in an adult from an endemic area - and it is the leading cause of acquired epilepsy worldwide

Also chronic headache, features of raised intracranial pressure with vomiting and papilloedema, and focal neurological deficits. subcutaneous and muscular cysticercosis presents as painless, firm, mobile nodules under the skin
Cognitive decline, confusion, personality change and dementia-like presentations
Visual disturbance, diplopia and visual field defects
Psychiatric symptoms including psychosis and depression
Intermittent obstructive hydrocephalus with positional headache and sudden collapse (BRUN'S syndrome) when a cyst floats freely in the ventricle
Myalgia and muscle swelling with a pseudohypertrophic appearance in heavy muscular involvement
Floaters, blurred vision and unilateral visual loss in ocular disease

Acquisition is by ingesting taenia solium eggs by the FAECO-ORAL route - from contaminated food, water or hands, from a household tapeworm carrier (who is often the source and may be asymptomatic), or by autoinfection - and not by eating pork, which causes intestinal taeniasis
Vegetarians and people who never eat pork can therefore develop cysticercosis, a point of considerable practical importance
New-onset partial seizures or generalized seizures associated with localized symptoms due to cysts in the brain or spinal cord

signs: GENERAL EXAMINATION may reveal firm, painless, mobile SUBCUTANEOUS NODULES 0.5-2 cm in diameter over the trunk, arms and thighs, which can be biopsied for definitive diagnosis. NEUROLOGICAL examination varies from entirely normal (common in parenchymal disease presenting only with seizures) to focal deficits, cranial nerve palsies, cerebellar signs, papilloedema and reduced consciousness. FUNDOSCOPY IS MANDATORY IN EVERY SUSPECTED CASE, BOTH FOR PAPILLOEDEMA AND TO IDENTIFY AN INTRAOCULAR CYST, since giving anthelmintic therapy in the presence of an untreated ocular cyst can cause severe inflammation and blindness. IMAGING IS THE CORNERSTONE OF DIAGNOSIS: CT is excellent for demonstrating CALCIFIED lesions, which appear as small punctate calcifications, while MRI IS SUPERIOR for viable cysts, for cysts in the ventricles, basal cisterns, brainstem and spinal cord, and for showing perilesional oedema
the classical appearance is a small round CYSTIC LESION CONTAINING AN ECCENTRIC HYPERDENSE MURAL NODULE - THE SCOLEX - which gives the pathognomonic 'HOLE-WITH-DOT' OR 'STARRY SKY' APPEARANCE
lesions are staged as VESICULAR (viable, no enhancement or oedema), COLLOIDAL VESICULAR (degenerating, ring-enhancing with surrounding oedema), GRANULAR NODULAR, and finally CALCIFIED (dead)

muscle radiographs may show characteristic 'RICE GRAIN' or cigar-shaped calcifications. SEROLOGY by ENZYME-LINKED IMMUNOELECTROTRANSFER BLOT (EITB) using lentil lectin-purified glycoprotein antigens is far more specific than ELISA, though it is INSENSITIVE IN SINGLE-LESION AND CALCIFIED-ONLY DISEASE
CSF may show lymphocytic pleocytosis with EOSINOPHILS, raised protein and LOW GLUCOSE in subarachnoid disease
DEL BRUTTO'S REVISED DIAGNOSTIC CRITERIA combine absolute, major, minor and epidemiological criteria
ALWAYS EXAMINE THE STOOL OF THE PATIENT AND OF HOUSEHOLD MEMBERS FOR TAENIA EGGS AND PROGLOTTIDS
Signs of raised intracranial pressure, including papilledema, nausea, vomiting, and altered mental status may be present in advanced cases.
